newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Briton, Frenchman to be named to senior U.N. posts.
newsitem.headline: Briton, Frenchman to be named to senior U.N. posts.

text.p: A British diplomat, Sir Kieran Prendergast, is expected to be named on Tuesday as under-secretary-general for political affairs, one of the most senior posts in the U.N. secretariat, a U.N. source said on Monday.
The appointment will be among more than a dozen to be announced by Secretary-General Kofi Annan, who succeeded Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Jan. 1 and is now assembling his own team of top officials.
Another appointment is likely to be that of French diplomat Bernard Miyet as under-secretary-general in charge of U.N. peacekeeping operations, the source added.
This is the post held by Annan before his election last month as secretary-general.
Miyet is France's representative to the Vienna-based Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe.
Prendergast has served most recently as Britain's ambassador to Turkey and before that as high commissioner to Kenya.
In the late 1970s he was a member of Britain's U.N. mission in New York.

He would succeed Under-Secretary-General Marrack Goulding who, as head of the U.N. department of political affairs since March 1993, is the most senior Briton in the U.N. secretariat. He previously headed U.N. peacekeeping.
Goulding, who joined the United Nations in 1986 after a career with the British foreign service, is to take up an appointment later this year as Warden of St Antony's College, Oxford.
